title: The viewer writes a site when traces are wanted, and nothing on record says so
foundBy: repository owner, deciding to keep the folder form after a week of using it: "agreed on keeping the folder"
details:
**What exists.** Since the traces branch, `cs-dispatch-viewer` draws each member's trace inside its dispatch boxes. Every step and anchor on the timeline is meant to link to its event in the trace, and a link needs a page to land on. So when `-o` names a directory, the viewer writes a site: the dispatch page as `index.html`, and the tracer's own export of every session under `tracer/`, one page per trace. A single-file render still carries the trace data, and has no links.

**What was missing.** `SPEC.md` said the viewer writes one file, and no record said the folder form exists or why it was chosen over baking the traces into the page. The owner held both back until they had used it.

**Why the folder.** On run14-1 the page is about 1 MB and the tracer's export about 7 MB across 16 traces; baked in, the page would parse all of it before showing anything. The trace pages are the tracer's, made by `cs-tracer` at render time from the archive's raw evidence. So the viewer learns nothing CLI-specific, and a newer tracer can re-read an old archive. And the links need real pages. The cost is that a folder is passed around by zipping or serving it, which suits a tool whose readers are the owner and the agents.

**What to do.** Say so in `SPEC.md`, and keep this record as the decision.
